messages:
maria: Running a quick nsys capture on the KV prefetch path inside k8s and the kernel selection looks wrong — we keep falling back to a generic gemm when short sequences hit.

sam: hmm, did you run with the container privileged? last time we saw missing CUPTI markers when toolkit couldn't attach.

maria: not privileged. used the default DaemonSet with nvidia.com/gpu and securityContext:restricted. capture output shows no NVTX ranges in timeline.

kevin: NVTX missing often means the profiler can't read CUPTI. nsys still records CUDA kernels but attributes a lot to low-level memcpy/gemm. can you paste the nsys command?

maria: running: ```nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=cpu,gpu --stats=true --capture-range=gpu_task ./serve --profile-kv=on```

carla: also check /dev/nvidia-uvm and /dev/nvidia-modeset devices inside the pod. toolkit needs access to them or the CUPTI lib will fail open.

maria: confirmed /dev/nvidia-uvm not present in the pod. DaemonSet mounts were missing devicePlugin config.

sam: that would do it. Two options: 1) run the profiler pods with hostDevices/devices added and cap SYS_PTRACE, or 2) run nsys on the node (hostPID/hostNetwork) to avoid container restrictions. For k8s, here's a minimal securityContext we used: ```securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: true
  capabilities:
    add: ["SYS_ADMIN","SYS_PTRACE"]
  devices:
    - name: nvidia-uvm
      hostPath: /dev/nvidia-uvm
```

kevin: FYI, we saw a perf regression last week where batching heuristics changed kernel selection — if CUPTI is absent we mis-detect sequence grouping and that triggers a fallback GEMM that dominates time. So missing NVTX can mask whether batching is working.

maria: thanks, added devices and reran. NVTX ranges show up now but I still see a weird hotspot at 1.2s in the timeline that corresponds to a kernel called matmul_generic.

carla: can you share the perfetto link? or paste the kernel timeline snippet. sometimes a tiny change in launch bounds yields a different kernel variant.

maria: perfetto capture: https://perfetto.dev/trace/viewer?utm_source=local&trace=/tmp/trace1.pbz (local link)

maria: timeline snippet: ```
[ 0.95s ] nvtx:batch_start
[ 0.96s ] kernel: matmul_tiled_32x32 (expected)
[ 0.98s ] kernel: matmul_generic (unexpected, 250ms)  <-- hotspot
[ 1.25s ] nvtx:batch_end
```

sam: that generic kernel suggests we hit an unsupported tile size at runtime. Could be int8 quant path falling back because cuBLAS/forged kernel selection couldn't find optimized kernels for the current sequence length distribution. Are you running with our quantization profile?

maria: yes quant profile is enabled. I compared with a golden trace from Dedicated where matmul_tiled_32x32 is used consistently. In k8s it flips.

kevin: check kernel driver versions and libcublas versions inside the node. Also ensure we aren't accidentally binding to a CPU affinity that forces different launch parameters. I once saw scheduler noise causing different warmup and a fallback.

carla: another thing — file permissions on the CUPTI socket/cache dir can prevent kernel registry lookups which triggers fallback. Ensure /tmp/cupti_cache (or /var/tmp) is writable by the container user. We had a case where the container ran as non-root and couldn't write the kernel signature cache, so every launch missed the fast path.

maria: aha, /var/tmp/cupti_cache was owned root:root and mode 700. changing to uid 1000 and 770 fixed it locally. retesting now.

perf-bot: deploy-check: nsight-runner pod updated with device mounts and adjusted permissions. CI perf baseline diff: +0.9% latency p50, investigating.

maria: new trace shows matmul_tiled reappearing and the 250ms hotspot is gone. KV prefetch batching now groups ~6 sequences instead of 2, latency stable.

sam: great. Action items: (1) update k8s profiler DaemonSet to mount nvidia devices and set SYS_PTRACE cap, (2) ensure cupti cache dirs are writable in our runtime image (we should set TMPDIR to /tmp/run and chown during image build), (3) add a quick profiler preflight check that validates NVTX/CUPTI visibility and device nodes.

carla: I'll open a PR to add the preflight check and doc the securityContext snippet.

maria: thanks all. leaving the perftrace and capture commands in the thread for future runs.```
